subject.title: Cron sessions deliver hallucinated output instead of failing cleanly when tool calls fail

question: What fail-closed contract should unattended cron delivery use when a run has unrecovered tool errors, missing required tool calls, or unverifiable final output?
rationale: Current source has diagnostic and fatal-structured-error handling, but it intentionally permits some recovered/non-terminal warnings and final assistant text; maintainers must choose the default delivery semantics and the boundary between core cron safety and plugin claim-verification policy.

options.title: Narrow core cron fail-closed invariant
options.body: Suppress normal cron delivery and record or alert failure when known tool errors or required tool evidence remain unrecovered, without adding broad regex-based claim verification to core.

options.title: Plugin-only claim verification boundary
options.body: Keep core limited to structured fatal signals and route all unsupported success-claim checking to ClawHub/plugin implementations.

options.title: Defer to native recovery work
options.body: Wait for the broader native tool-failure recovery design and document the current unattended cron risk meanwhile.

recommendation.title: Narrow core cron fail-closed invariant
recommendation.body: Suppress normal cron delivery and record or alert failure when known tool errors or required tool evidence remain unrecovered, without adding broad regex-based claim verification to core.
